entries.title: How do I enter student marks?
entries.content:
To enter examination marks in the Marks Schedule system:

Log in with your staff username and password.
Select the academic year.
Select the term: 1st Term, 2nd Term, or 3rd Term.
Select the required class.
Find the student and subject.
Click the marks cell.
Enter a mark from 0 to 100, or enter Ab for absent.
Press Enter, Tab, or click outside the cell to save the change temporarily.
Check the student's total, average, and rank.
Click Save to save the marks to the school database.

entries.title: What does Ab mean in marks entry?
entries.content: In the Marks Schedule system, Ab means the student was absent for that subject. Enter Ab in the student's subject marks cell.

entries.title: What are the mark grades used by the system?
entries.content:
The Marks Schedule system displays marks using these ranges:

75–100: A
60–below 75: B
45–below 60: C
Above 35 and below 45: S
35 or below: W
Ab: Absent

entries.title: How do I log in to the Marks Schedule system?
entries.content: To log in to the Marks Schedule system, enter your staff username and password and sign in. After successful authentication, select the academic year and then select the term: 1st Term, 2nd Term, or 3rd Term. Confirm the period to enter the marks workspace.

entries.title: What does Class Teacher Of do?
entries.content: In Teacher Management, Class Teacher Of assigns a teacher to a class. In the Marks Schedule system, a class teacher assignment gives that teacher full marks-editing access for every subject in the assigned class.

entries.title: What does Subject Taught do?
entries.content: Subject Taught identifies the subject assigned to a staff member. In the Marks Schedule system, a teacher assigned to a subject can edit that subject's marks in classes where that subject is available.

entries.title: Can a teacher have both class and subject permissions?
entries.content: Yes. Class and subject assignments stack. For example, assigning a teacher to Grade 11 as Class Teacher Of gives full editing access to every subject in Grade 11, while also assigning Maths gives Maths editing access in other classes where Maths appears.

entries.title: Why can I see marks but cannot edit them?
entries.content: Marks editing depends on the staff member's role and assignment. A Principal has full marks editing access. A class teacher can edit all subjects in the assigned class. A subject teacher can edit their assigned subject in classes where that subject is available. If a mark is visible but not editable, the account may not have the required class or subject permission.

entries.title: How do I save marks after entering them?
entries.content: After changing marks, the Save button appears in the Marks Schedule system. Click Save to write the marks to the school database. A successful save displays a confirmation. If there are unsaved marks, the system warns before logout.

entries.title: How do I submit today's student attendance count?
entries.content:
To submit today's class student count:

1. Open the attendance page for the class.
2. Confirm the class and today's date.
3. Optionally enter the teacher or staff name.
4. Enter the number of boys.
5. Enter the number of girls.
6. The system automatically calculates the total students.
7. Click SUBMIT TODAY'S COUNT.

The system checks that the values are valid whole numbers and prevents a duplicate first submission for the same class and date.

entries.title: How do I edit today's attendance count?
entries.content:
When today's attendance count already exists, staff can edit it after authentication:

1. Open the class attendance page.
2. Use Staff Login.
3. Sign in with your staff username and password.
4. Change the boys and/or girls count.
5. Check the automatically recalculated total.
6. Click SAVE CHANGES.

entries.title: What numbers can I enter for attendance?
entries.content: Attendance boys and girls fields must contain whole numbers. Blank values are rejected, negative numbers are rejected, and unreasonable values above the system's configured maximum are rejected. The total is automatically calculated as boys plus girls.

entries.title: Why can't I submit the same attendance count twice?
entries.content: The attendance system stores one daily count record for each class and date. A new first submission is prevented when a record for that class and date already exists. To change an existing submission, use the staff editing process instead.

entries.title: How do I use Staff Login to edit attendance?
entries.content: When an existing daily attendance count needs to be edited, open Staff Login on the class attendance page. Enter the staff username and password, click Sign in, and then edit the boys and girls values. Click SAVE CHANGES to update the record.

entries.title: What can the attendance administrator see?
entries.content: The attendance administrator interface provides school-wide daily student-count information, including class submission status, boys, girls, total students, submitted and missing class counts, CSV export, printable reports, class comparison, analytics, attendance trend charts, and QR codes for class daily-count pages.

entries.title: How do I log in to Teacher Management?
entries.content: Open Hindu Teacher Management, enter the administrator username and password, and click Login. A successful login opens the administrator dashboard. The assistant should not disclose passwords; use administrator-provided credentials.

entries.title: How do I add a new teacher or staff member?
entries.content:
To add a staff member in Teacher Management:

1. Open Add Staff.
2. Enter the full name.
3. Select the role.
4. Optionally select Class Teacher Of.
5. Optionally select Subject Taught.
6. Fill in the required staff details.
7. Use the auto-generated username and password, or edit them.
8. Use Regenerate Username/Password when new credentials are needed.
9. Click Save Staff Member.
10. The system checks that the username is not already in use.
11. After successful creation, the generated username and password are displayed so the administrator can share them with the staff member.

entries.title: What staff roles are available in Teacher Management?
entries.content: Teacher Management provides these roles: Principal, Deputy Principal, Vice Principal, Sectional Head, and Teacher.

entries.title: What information can I enter for a staff member?
entries.content: The Teacher Management staff form can contain Full Name, Role, Date of Birth, Gender, Employee/NIC No., Phone Number, Qualification, Date Joined, Address, Class Teacher Of, Subject Taught, Username, and Password.

entries.title: How do I edit a teacher or staff member?
entries.content: Find the staff member in the All Staff list, open the edit action, change the required fields, and click Save Changes. The staff record is then updated in the school database.

entries.title: Can an administrator delete a staff record?
entries.content: Yes. The Teacher Management administrator interface includes a delete action for staff records.

entries.title: Why do Teacher Management class and subject lists match the Marks Schedule?
entries.content: Teacher Management loads current class names and live subject information from the Firestore classes collection used by the Marks Schedule system. This connects the staff class/subject assignments with the academic marks system.

entries.title: What happens if the Marks Schedule database cannot be reached?
entries.content: If the Marks Schedule cannot reach the marks database while loading, it can fall back to locally saved marks where available and show a warning. Saving updated marks to the school database requires database connectivity.

entries.title: What should I do if the attendance page cannot load the class?
entries.content: If the attendance class cannot be found, choose the correct class or ask the school office to verify the class list. If a class is inactive, contact the school office. If the database cannot be reached, check the internet connection and retry.

entries.title: What should I do if I forget my staff username or password?
entries.content: The supplied systems do not show a documented self-service password-reset workflow. Contact the school administrator (Sudharshan Sir)responsible for Teacher Management so the staff account can be checked or updated.
